groups.text:
For each question from 16 to 20, choose the word closest in meaning to the underlined words.

Last Saturday, my classmates and I attended an environmental awareness talk at a community club. During the session, the speaker explained how plastic pollution was harming marine life. I was shocked to learn that many sea animals become __(16: entangled)__ in plastic waste or mistake it for food. It was __(17: alarming)__ to hear that millions of tonnes of plastic enter the oceans every year.
After the talk, my friend Ben and I were inspired to make a change. We both __(18: took up)__ simple habits, such as bringing reusable water bottles, metal straws and shopping bags whenever we went out. Our teacher reminded us that every small action mattered. I realised that making these __(19: important)__ changes would help reduce plastic waste in the world.
Since then, I have __(20: consistently)__ avoided single-use plastics and encouraged my family to do the same. Together, we can protect marine life and keep our environment clean for future generations.

Study the information for an event (Text 1) and the extract from a school newsletter (Text 2) and answer questions 21 to 25.

++Text 1++
The text below provides information for an event.
[[img1]]
++Text 2++
The extract below, from a school newsletter, is a pupil's thoughts about the upcoming school park run.
The annual park run is not just about running. It is about coming together as a school community to get active and have fun. When we all join in, whether we are fast or slow, we learn to support one another. Even when it is tough, we keep going because we know our friends are there to cheer us on. Winning is not the only goal. It is also about self-motivation to complete the entire course from start to end and having a sense of achievement as a result.
Running with our classmates makes us feel like we are part of something big and exciting. We show determination, encourage one another and feel a sense of pride. Moreover, it's a great way to stay fit. With each step, we are building our endurance and growing stronger, both physically and mentally.
So, let's hit the trail and embrace the adventure of the park run! Together, we will run, laugh and make memories that will last a lifetime.

groups.text:
There are 10 blanks, numbered 26 to 35, in the passage below. From the list of words given, choose the most suitable word for each blank. Write its letter (A to Q) in the blank. The letters (I) and (O) have been omitted to avoid confusion during marking.
**EACH WORD CAN BE USED ONLY ONCE.**
[[table1]]

The Changi Chapel and Museum stands as a reminder of Singapore's wartime history. Originally opened in 2001, the museum underwent __(26)__ extensive revamp to modernise itself. It serves to honour the prisoners of war (POWs) and civilians __(27)__ were held in the Changi area during the Japanese Occupation.
The original chapel was built __(28)__ POWs during their imprisonment. These brave individuals used whatever materials they could find, such as attap leaves and scrap metal, to construct a place of worship. The chapel provided a crucial sanctuary where prisoners __(29)__ find comfort amidst harsh conditions. Today, a faithful replica of the chapel sits in the open-air area of the museum, allowing visitors a quiet space __(30)__ reflection.
The main exhibition area is home __(31)__ a massive collection of personal items, photographs, and letters donated by the survivors and their families. Every artefact has __(32)__ own story of resilience __(33)__ has been preserved for future generations. For example, visitors can view secret messages hidden within everyday objects, demonstrating the creativity of the prisoners.
Anyone who is interested in history __(34)__ make a visit to this site. It bridges the gap __(35)__ the painful past and the peaceful present, teaching the younger generation the true value of psychological defence and strength.
Adapted from https://www.heritage.sg/changichapelmuseum

Each of the underlined words contains either a spelling or grammatical error. Write the correct word in each of the boxes.

Ever since Max became a teenager, his parents had given him money on his birthday instead of buying him presents. As he was __(36: turnind)__ twenty-one, he requested his mother, Andrea, to donate any money he got to charity. Andrea thought of an idea. She borrowed a video camera to __(37: documentary)__ the day. Then, she withdrew 21 ten-dollar notes from the bank and bought 21 apples.
When they spotted a homeless man down the street, Andrea approached him kindly. "Today is my son Max's 21st birthday. To __(38: sellerbrait)__, he asked me to give a gift to someone," she said. She then handed the man a ten-dollar note and an apple. The man smiled into the camera and __(39: aknowleged)__ the gift with a hearty, "Happy birthday, Max!"
Next, Andrea repeated the __(40: jescher)__ with the men and women at a nearby charity kitchen. __(41: By)__ unison, they sang 'Happy Birthday' for the camera. Andrea then gave fifty dollars to a pizza parlour, although the staff were confused even after Andrea's __(42: explain)__. They wanted to give her a __(43: reseet)__ but she refused. Instead, she urged the owners to feed the hungry. "Happy birthday, Max!" the staff shouted, thanking him for his __(44: generous)__.
Andrea's final stop was her sister's office. Laughing at the __(45: bezdar)__ idea, her sister shouted into the camera, "Happy birthday, Max!"
Max loved the video and thought it was the best birthday gift ever!

Fill in the blanks with a suitable word.

Dementia is a condition that affects the brain. It can cause problems with memory, thinking and communication. The 2023 Well-being of the Singapore Elderly (WiSE) study by the Institute of Mental Health found __(46)__ about one in 11 individuals aged 60 and above __(47)__ dementia. Many people think dementia __(48)__ causes memory loss but it can also lead to changes in behaviour and personality.
Caring for a loved one with dementia can be overwhelming. This is especially true when there are behavioural changes and communication problems. Some people with dementia may __(49)__ restless, suspicious or easily upset. These changes can be difficult for family members and caregivers to understand. When a loved one with dementia behaves in a __(50)__ that seems unusual, it is important to remember that the person is often __(51)__ to communicate a need or feeling. __(52)__ dementia affects the brain, they may find it difficult to express themselves __(53)__ with words.
A person with dementia may repeatedly ask for food even though they have __(54)__ eaten. This happens because they cannot __(55)__ having their meal. Others may refuse to shower or groom themselves, while some may stay __(56)__ at night and feel sleepy during the day.
A person with dementia may use the wrong word or describe an object instead of naming it directly. They may become frustrated when they are trying to find the __(57)__ words. Frustration can affect their confidence and mood. To help people with dementia, caregivers should remain patient and supportive. Experts recommend using a gentle approach and paying __(58)__ to the person's emotions. Instead of dismissing __(59)__ concerns, caregivers should recognise how they feel and try to understand their unmet needs.
It is also helpful to use short and simple sentences. Most importantly, caregivers should speak calmly and offer reassurance when __(60)__. With the right support, people with dementia can continue to feel respected, valued and included in their families and communities.
Adapted from https://www.imh.com.sg/Mental-Heal resources/Conditions-

Read the passage and answer questions 66 to 75.

**1** Twelve-year-old Darto sat under a banyan tree with his friends Arif and Siti. Life moved slowly in their quiet village—far too slowly for Darto, whose imagination could power a small city. If there was ever trouble, the villagers knew there was a good chance he had something to do with it. Moreover, much to their annoyance, Darto insisted on chasing and frightening their chickens.
**2** Arif said, "Uncle Banu has a chicken that cannot be caught. He calls it Putih."
**3** "Can't be caught? Ha! Catching Putih will be easy! Then everyone will admit I am the best chicken chaser in the village!" Darto exclaimed, jumping to his feet, his eyes lit up.
**4** That night, Darto, followed by his friends, crept quietly into Uncle Banu's yard. There, he saw a sleek, white bird pecking at the ground near the coop. Just then, the lights in Uncle Banu's house turned on. Darto froze, his heart beating so fast he thought it might burst. For a while nothing happened. He kept an eye on the house and made his move only when he saw the lights go out. Darto walked slowly towards Putih, his hands stretched out towards it, trying to appear as harmless as possible.
**5** As soon as it spotted Darto, Putih fixed its gaze on him and cocked its head. Then, as though realising his true intentions, Putih bolted. Darto scrambled after the bird as it darted through the yard like a feathery lightning bolt, weaving between banana trees and leaping over piles of firewood. Darto stayed close behind, but the chicken was faster—and far cleverer. It led him into a muddy ditch, then through a thorny bush that left his arms covered in scratches. By the time he emerged, he was exhausted, bleeding and coated in mud.
**6** "I told you he couldn't do it!" shouted Siti. Arif and Siti were laughing so hard they could barely breathe. Cheeks burning, Darto glared at his friends, then at the Putih, who was perched smugly on the roof of Uncle Banu's goat shed. It was clear that Putih was no ordinary chicken and could not be underestimated. However, it was he, Darto, who would have the final victory! If he could not outrun it, then he would outsmart it!
**7** The next day, Darto borrowed a fishing net from his aunt and a handful of corn from his mother. When he reached the chicken yard, he saw a crowd of children. Unknown to Darto, word of his mission had spread through the village thanks to Arif and Siti. They cheered him on as if he were a hero in a great battle. Even Uncle Banu was there. Darto's stomach fluttered at the sight of so many eyes on him. However, Darto waved to **his audience**, smiled, and loudly declared that Putih had no chance.
**8** Darto scattered the corn near the chicken coop and hid, holding the net at the ready. After several minutes, Putih appeared. It approached the corn cautiously, pecking at the ground, but always kept its distance. Losing patience, Darto lunged forward, throwing the net with all his might. But Putih was too far away, and the net landed uselessly on the ground. Then, with a loud squawk, it launched itself at Darto, claws outstretched. Darto dodged and ran for his life.
**9** "Help!" Darto screamed, running in circles as the chicken chased him, the crowd roaring with laughter. Exhausted, Darto was finally ready to admit defeat. Head hung low, he went to Uncle Banu to apologise, expecting a scolding.
**10** To his surprise, Uncle Banu simply laughed and ruffled his hair. "There is no shame losing to Putih, you know. My grandfather raised it from an egg and it's been keeping me on my toes ever since."
**11** Darto blinked. "Wait . . . how old is Putih?"
**12** Uncle Banu smiled. "Older than you'd believe."
**13** Trying to catch Putih became something of a tradition among the children after that. Even Darto made several more attempts. Although he never did catch Putih, he did not mind. He realised that the chase was more fun than the catch. From that day on, whenever Putih strutted through the village, clucking like it owned the place, Darto could not help but smile.
**14** Because in his village even a chicken could be a legend.
Adapted from "The Chicken Chase of Banyumas" by Fendy S. Tulodo

questions.stem: Ahmad saw a robber __________ a neighbour's house while he was out for a walk.

explanation: Rule: after a verb of the senses (see, hear, watch, feel) + a person or thing, use the base form of the verb (or the -ing form): 'I saw him **leave**', 'We heard her **sing**'.
'saw' already carries the past tense, so the second verb does not take a tense. That rules out 'enters', 'entered' and 'has entered'.
'entered' is tempting because the sentence is in the past, but 'saw a robber entered' is wrong.
'Ahmad saw a robber enter a neighbour's house.' The answer is option (1).

questions.stem: The team __________ for hours when the coach called for a break.

explanation: Two past events: the training started first and was still going on when the coach called for a break.
Rule: for an action that had been going on for some time ('for hours') up to another past moment, use the past perfect continuous: had been + verb-ing.
'has been training' is the present form and does not match the past verb 'called'. 'had trained' is tempting, but it does not show that the action continued over those hours until the break.
'The team had been training for hours when the coach called for a break.' The answer is option (3).

questions.stem: "He's been an actor in a play, __________ ?" said Lisa.

explanation: First work out what 'He's' stands for. It is followed by 'been', a past participle, so it is 'He **has** been', not 'He is'.
Rule: a question tag repeats the helping verb of the statement. A positive statement takes a negative tag.
Helping verb 'has', positive statement, so the tag is 'hasn't he'.
'isn't he' is the trap for pupils who read 'He's' as 'He is'. The answer is option (3).

questions.stem: I was not sure if Henry and Betty could complete the difficult task by __________.

explanation: 'by + reflexive pronoun' means alone, without help. The reflexive pronoun must match the people doing the action.
Who would complete the task? 'Henry and Betty', two people who are not the speaker, so the pronoun is 'they' and its reflexive form is 'themselves'.
'myself' is tempting because the sentence begins with 'I', but 'I' is only the one who was not sure, not the one doing the task.
The answer is option (4), themselves.

questions.stem: The flock of crows __________ becoming a nuisance, which forced my father to call the authorities.

explanation: Find the real subject. In 'The flock of crows', the head word is 'flock', which is one group, so the verb is singular. 'crows' only tells us what kind of flock. That rules out 'are' and 'were'.
Now the tense. The second half says 'which **forced** my father', which is past, so the first verb must be past too.
Singular and past gives 'was'. 'were' is the trap for pupils who make the verb agree with the nearest noun, 'crows'.
'The flock of crows was becoming a nuisance.' The answer is option (3).

questions.stem: There was __________ warning before the rollercoaster suddenly plunged downwards, causing my sister to scream.

explanation: 'warning' here is an uncountable noun (we say 'There **was** ... warning'), so 'few', which goes with countable plural nouns, is out.
Meaning: the rollercoaster plunged 'suddenly' and the sister screamed, so there was hardly any warning.
'little' means almost none and goes with uncountable nouns. 'much' and 'enough' would mean there was plenty of warning, which does not fit 'suddenly'.
'There was little warning.' The answer is option (2).

questions.stem: Surrounded by strangers at the party, the shy little girl hid __________ her parents the whole time.

explanation: The girl was shy and surrounded by strangers, so she used her parents as a shield. To hide **behind** someone is to stay at the back of them so that others cannot see you.
'hid from her parents' would mean she did not want her parents to find her, which does not fit a child frightened of strangers.
'beside' means next to, where she would still be seen. 'among' is for a group of three or more.
The answer is option (2), behind.

questions.stem: The man was arrested for driving __________ the influence of alcohol.

explanation: This is a fixed phrase: **under the influence of** something means affected or controlled by it.
We say 'driving under the influence of alcohol' and 'under the influence of his friends'.
'with', 'on' and 'against' do not go with 'the influence of' to give this meaning.
The answer is option (3), under.

questions.stem: Did the famous director choose all the movies __________ at the film festival last year?

explanation: The blank describes 'the movies'. The full form is 'all the movies **that were shown** at the film festival'.
Movies do not show anything; they are shown by people. That is the passive, which needs the past participle. When 'that were' is dropped, only the past participle stays: 'the movies shown'.
The past participle of 'show' is 'shown'. 'showed' is the simple past form, and 'showing' would mean the movies were doing the showing.
The answer is option (2), shown.

questions.stem: I realised that I would have failed __________ my mother's good advice. It was a good thing I listened to her.

explanation: 'would have failed' talks about something that did **not** happen. The second sentence confirms it: the speaker listened to the advice, so he did not fail.
'if not for' means 'if it had not been for' or 'without': without my mother's advice, I would have failed.
'because of' would mean the advice caused the failure. 'in spite of' would mean he failed even though he had good advice. Both go against the second sentence.
The answer is option (1), if not for.

questions.stem: Most shopping malls in Singapore are __________ by MRT or bus.

explanation: Clue: 'by MRT or bus' tells us how people get to the malls.
'accessible' means able to be reached or entered: a place is accessible by train, by road or on foot.
'available' means ready to be used or bought, and is not used with 'by MRT'. 'attainable' is for goals that can be achieved. 'approachable' describes a friendly person who is easy to talk to.
The answer is option (3), accessible.

questions.stem: Arun is a/an __________ team member. When his group did not have enough materials for their Science project, he came up with the idea of using plastic bottles to complete their model.

explanation: Clue: the group lacked materials and Arun 'came up with the idea of using plastic bottles'. He solved a problem with what was at hand.
'resourceful' means good at finding clever ways to deal with difficulties, especially when you have little to work with.

'industrious' means hardworking, but nothing says he worked hard. 'collaborative' means working well with others, and 'exceptional' means outstanding in general; neither points to finding a clever solution.
The answer is option (1), resourceful.

questions.stem: "While we cannot say for sure, the time needed to recover after a serious case of food poisoning is __________ one week," added the doctor.

explanation: Clue: 'While we cannot say for sure'. The doctor is giving a usual figure, not a precise one.
'generally' means usually, in most cases.
'exactly' and 'specifically' both mean precisely, which contradicts 'cannot say for sure'. 'constantly' means all the time, without stopping.
The answer is option (2), generally.

questions.stem: After applying some ointment on my injured elbow, the pain slowly __________. I was able to bend my arm again after some time.

explanation: Clue: the writer could bend the arm again, so the pain went away bit by bit.
'wear off' is used for a feeling or an effect that gradually disappears: the pain wore off, the medicine wore off.

'wear on' means time passes slowly ('as the day wore on'). 'wear out' means to become useless from use, or to make someone very tired. 'wear away' is for a surface that becomes thinner through rubbing, like stone steps.
The answer is option (2), wore off.

questions.stem: Marine biologists are studying the long term __________ of a tsunami on coastal habitats.

explanation: Clues: 'long term' and 'on coastal habitats'. We need a word for the effects that something is likely to have on something else in the future.
'implications' means the possible effects or consequences of an event. It is used in the pattern 'the implications of X on/for Y'.

'results' and 'outcomes' are tempting, but they name how something finally turns out (the result of a match, the outcome of a meeting) and are not followed by 'on' something. 'inferences' are conclusions a person works out from clues.
The answer is option (4), implications.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++entangled++.

explanation: To be 'entangled' in something is to be caught and twisted up in it so that you cannot get free, like a turtle caught in a fishing net.
In the passage, sea animals 'become entangled in plastic waste', which harms them because they cannot escape.
'trapped' means caught and unable to get away, which matches.
'buried', 'hidden' and 'concealed' are all about being covered or out of sight, not about being unable to move. The answer is option (3).

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++alarming++.

explanation: 'alarming' means causing worry or fear.
The writer heard that 'millions of tonnes of plastic enter the oceans every year', news that is worrying and upsetting.
'distressing' means causing worry or upset, which matches.

'surprising' is tempting, but a surprise can be pleasant and carries no worry. 'stunning' usually means very impressive, and 'depressing' means making you feel sad and hopeless. The answer is option (3).

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++took up++.

explanation: To 'take up' a habit or a hobby is to start doing it.
The writer and Ben 'took up simple habits, such as bringing reusable water bottles': they started these new habits after the talk.
'adopted' means started to use or follow something new (to adopt a habit), which matches.
'practised' is tempting, but it means doing something again and again, not starting it. 'utilised' means made use of a thing. The answer is option (2).

review.note: The key's digit for Q18 lies on the watermark; it reads 2 (white digit on black), which matches the solved answer.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++important++.

explanation: 'important' here means mattering a lot, having a big effect.
Just before this, the teacher said that 'every small action mattered'. These changes matter because they 'would help reduce plastic waste'.
'significant' means important and having a noticeable effect, which matches.
'essential' is tempting, but it is stronger: it means absolutely necessary, something you cannot do without. 'prominent' means well known or easily seen. The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++consistently++.

explanation: 'consistently' means in the same way every time, without changing.
'Since then, I have consistently avoided single-use plastics': the writer has kept the habit up all the time since the talk.
'regularly' means happening again and again as a habit, which is closest.
'intermittently' is the opposite: stopping and starting. 'deliberately' means on purpose. The answer is option (2).

questions.stem: "Ready for our school's Park Run?" Why did the writer ask this question in Text 1?
options: to share the purpose of the run
to get pupils excited before the run
to invite pupils to take part in the run
to mentally prepare pupils for the run

explanation: The question is the big heading of Text 1. A heading that speaks directly to the reader in a lively way is there to catch attention and build excitement.
(1) is wrong because the purpose is given separately under 'Objectives of the run'.
(3) is tempting, but pupils are not being invited: Text 1 gives a reporting time and tells Primary 3 to 6 pupils where to assemble, so the run is for all of them. There is nothing to sign up for.
The answer is option (2).

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true of the run?
options: This is the first year it is being held.
The venue is West Coast Primary School.
Pupils from Primary 1 to 6 will participate in it.
All pupils will complete the run at the same point.

explanation: Check each statement against Text 1.

(1) is false: it is the '5th Annual Park Run'. (2) is false: pupils assemble in school and then set off for 'Elizabeth Gardens', where the run is held. (3) is false: 'Primary 1 and 2 pupils will remain in school for the Sports Carnival'.
(4) is true: the route map shows two start lines (one for Primary 3, one for Primary 4-6) but only one 'FINISH LINE'.
The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: Based on text 2, which of the following is ++not++ mentioned as a benefit of taking part in the park run?
options: feeling a sense of pride for the school

explanation: Look for each option in Text 2.
'we are building our endurance and growing stronger, both physically and mentally' covers (1) and (2). 'feel a sense of pride' covers (4).
Medals and prizes are never mentioned. In fact the writer says 'Winning is not the only goal.'
The answer is option (3).

review.note: The key's digit for Q23 is partly under the watermark; the visible strokes are a 3, which matches the solved answer.

questions.stem: In text 2, what does the writer mean by "part of something big and exciting"?
options: Pupils are part of a race as a full school.
Pupils are excited to run with their friends.
Pupils are running in a famous park that is big.
Pupils are taking part in an exciting event as a community.

explanation: Read the whole sentence: 'Running with our classmates makes us feel like we are part of something big and exciting.' Earlier the writer says the run 'is about coming together as a school community'.
So 'something big' is the event shared by many people, and being 'part of' it means belonging to that community.

(1) is wrong on two counts: the writer says it 'is not just about running' and winning is not the only goal, so it is not simply a race, and Primary 1 and 2 do not run, so it is not the full school. (3) is about the size of the park, which is not what 'big' refers to.
The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: Which idea is expressed in ++both++ Text 1 and Text 2?
options: Pupils should encourage peers who are slow runners.
Running with friends helps to create lasting memories.
Running as a school improves fitness and builds bonds.
Pupils get a sense of achievement from completing a run.

explanation: The idea must appear in both texts, so start with Text 1, which says less. Its objectives are 'to promote the physical well-being of pupils' and 'to foster school spirit'.
Text 2 says the same two things: 'it's a great way to stay fit' (fitness) and 'coming together as a school community', 'we learn to support one another' (bonds).
(1), (2) and (4) are found only in Text 2: cheering one another on, 'memories that will last a lifetime' and 'a sense of achievement'.
The answer is option (3).

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (26). (Type its letter, A to R.)

explanation: 'revamp' is a singular countable noun mentioned for the first time, so it needs 'a' or 'an'.
The article goes with the sound of the very next word. The next word is 'extensive', which begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an'.
The answer is (B) an: 'the museum underwent an extensive revamp'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (27). (Type its letter, A to R.)

explanation: The blank begins a clause that tells us more about 'the prisoners of war (POWs) and civilians'.
They are people, and they are the subject of 'were held', so the relative pronoun is 'who'. 'which' is for things and animals.
The answer is (Q) who: 'civilians who were held in the Changi area'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (28). (Type its letter, A to R.)

explanation: 'was built' is in the passive voice. The doer of the action in a passive sentence is introduced with 'by'.
Who built the chapel? The POWs. The next sentence confirms it: they 'used whatever materials they could find ... to construct a place of worship'.
'for' is tempting, but it would mean someone else built it for them. The answer is (E) by: 'built by POWs'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (29). (Type its letter, A to R.)

explanation: After the blank is the base verb 'find', so the blank needs a modal verb. The modals in the list are 'could' and 'should'.
The sentence is about the past ('provided') and about what the prisoners were able to do there, so we need the past form of 'can'.
'should' shows advice or duty and is needed for blank (34). The answer is (C) could: 'where prisoners could find comfort'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (30). (Type its letter, A to R.)

explanation: The blank links 'a quiet space' to 'reflection', which is what the space is used for.
'for' shows purpose: a room for meetings, a space for reflection.
The answer is (F) for: 'a quiet space for reflection'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (31). (Type its letter, A to R.)

explanation: This is a fixed phrase: a place is **home to** something when that thing is found or kept there.
For example: 'The zoo is home to more than 300 kinds of animals.'
The answer is (N) to: 'is home to a massive collection'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (32). (Type its letter, A to R.)

explanation: The blank comes before 'own story', so it needs a possessive word.
The owner is 'Every artefact'. 'Every' makes the noun singular, and an artefact is a thing, so the possessive is 'its'.
'their' is tempting, but it is for plural owners. The answer is (J) its: 'Every artefact has its own story'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (33). (Type its letter, A to R.)

explanation: The blank begins a clause that tells us more about the 'story of resilience': the story ___ has been preserved.
A story is a thing, so the relative pronoun is 'which'. 'who' is for people and is needed for blank (27).
The answer is 'which': 'its own story of resilience which has been preserved for future generations'.
In the word list this word is printed with the letter (R). The school's answer key calls it P, so type R (P is accepted too).

review.note: The word list on the paper labels the last column (N) to, (R) which, (Q) who, although the instruction says the letters run from A to Q. The key gives 'P' for Q33, and there is no (P) in the list; the box labelled (R) sits where (P) should be. The word is 'which' either way. The table is transcribed as printed, and R, P and 'which' are all accepted.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (34). (Type its letter, A to R.)

explanation: After the blank is the base verb 'make', so the blank needs a modal verb.
The writer is recommending the museum to history lovers. 'should' is used to give advice or a recommendation.
'could' is already used for blank (29) and only says it is possible. The answer is (L) should: 'Anyone who is interested in history should make a visit'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (35). (Type its letter, A to R.)

explanation: Look at what follows: 'the painful past **and** the peaceful present'. Two things joined by 'and'.
A gap is always 'between' two things: 'bridge the gap between A and B'.
The answer is (D) between.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (36) ++turnind++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. Say the sentence aloud: 'As he was ___ twenty-one'. The word we hear is 'turning'.
Rule: was/were + verb-ing makes the past continuous. The ending is spelt -ing.
turn + ing = turning. 'To turn twenty-one' means to reach the age of twenty-one.
The correct word is 'turning'.

review.note: The last letter of the underlined word is not clear in the scan: the underline runs through it and it could be read as 'turnind' or as 'turning'. Since every underlined word must contain an error, it is transcribed as 'turnind'. The answer, 'turning', is the same as the key's either way. The section header prints '(12 marks)', but there are only ten items (36 to 45), and the Booklet B total of 65 printed on the cover works out only with 10 marks (10 + 10 + 15 + 10 + 20). Each item is given 1 mark.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (37) ++documentary++.

explanation: This is a grammar error. Look at the word in front: 'to ___ the day'. After 'to' we need a verb in its base form.
'documentary' is a noun (a film about real events). The verb is 'document', which means to record something in writing, photographs or film.
'She borrowed a video camera to document the day.'
The correct word is 'document'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (38) ++sellerbrait++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. Sound it out: sel-uh-brayt. The word is what people do on a birthday.
It begins with a soft 'c' (as in 'cell'), not 's', and ends in '-ate' (as in 'gate').
c-e-l-e-b-r-a-t-e. A related word helps: celebr**ation**.
The correct word is 'celebrate'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (39) ++aknowleged++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The word means showed that he had noticed and was thankful for the gift.
Build it from 'knowledge': ac + knowledge + d. Two letters are easy to miss: the 'c' before the 'k', and the 'd' before the 'g'.
a-c-k-n-o-w-l-e-d-g-e-d.
The correct word is 'acknowledged'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (40) ++jescher++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. Sound it out: jes-cher. A gesture is an action done to show a feeling, here the kind act of giving a ten-dollar note and an apple.
The 'j' sound is spelt with a soft 'g' (as in 'gentle'), and the 'cher' sound at the end is spelt '-ture' (as in 'picture', 'nature').
g-e-s-t-u-r-e.
The correct word is 'gesture'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (41) ++By++.

explanation: This is a grammar error: the wrong preposition.
The fixed phrase is **in unison**, which means all together at the same time.
'In unison, they sang 'Happy Birthday' for the camera.' Start with a capital letter because it begins the sentence.
The correct word is 'In'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (42) ++explain++.

explanation: This is a grammar error. Look at the word in front: 'Andrea's ___'. After a possessive (Andrea's, his, my) we need a noun.
'explain' is a verb. Its noun form is 'explanation'.
Watch the spelling: the 'i' of 'explain' is dropped. expla**n**ation, not 'explaination'.
The correct word is 'explanation'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (43) ++reseet++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. Sound it out: ri-seet. It is the slip of paper a shop gives to show that money has been paid.
Three things to remember: a soft 'c', the rule 'i before e except after c' (so 'cei'), and a silent 'p' before the 't'.
r-e-c-e-i-p-t.
The correct word is 'receipt'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (44) ++generous++.

explanation: This is a grammar error. Look at the word in front: 'thanking him for his ___'. After 'his' we need a noun.
'generous' is an adjective. Its noun form is 'generosity'.
Watch the spelling: the 'u' is dropped. gener**os**ity, not 'generousity'.
The correct word is 'generosity'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (45) ++bezdar++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. Sound it out: bi-zar. It means very strange or unusual. Giving away money and apples for someone else's birthday was a very unusual idea.
One 'z', double 'r', and a silent 'e' at the end.
b-i-z-a-r-r-e.
The correct word is 'bizarre'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (46) with a suitable word.

explanation: After the reporting verb 'found' comes a whole clause that says what was found: 'about one in 11 individuals ... has dementia'.
The word that introduces such a clause is 'that': found that, said that, showed that.
The answer is 'that'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (47) with a suitable word.

explanation: The clause 'about one in 11 individuals aged 60 and above ___ dementia' has no verb yet. We say a person 'has' a condition.
The head of the subject is 'one' (one in 11), which is singular, so the verb is 'has'. The words 'individuals aged 60 and above' sit in between and must not decide the verb.
The present tense is used because this is still true today.
The answer is 'has'.

review.note: The key gives 'has' (the subject 'one in 11' taken as singular). 'have' is common in everyday use with 'one in 11 individuals', and 'had' agrees with the past verb 'found'; both are added to the accepted answers. A school marker may accept only 'has'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (48) with a suitable word.

explanation: Look at the second half of the sentence: 'but it can **also** lead to changes in behaviour and personality'.
'but ... also' tells us the first half limits dementia to one thing: many people think memory loss is all it causes.
The word that limits is 'only' (only ... but also).
The answer is 'only'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (49) with a suitable word.

explanation: After the modal 'may' we need a verb in its base form. After the blank are three adjectives: 'restless, suspicious or easily upset'.
A verb that links a person to an adjective describing a state is needed: feel, become, be.
'feel' fits best because these are emotions. 'become' also makes sense because the next sentence calls them 'changes'.
The answer is 'feel'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (50) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'behaves in a ___ that seems unusual': the blank is a singular noun after 'a'.
The fixed pattern is 'to behave in a way that ...' or 'in a manner that ...'.
The answer is 'way'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (51) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'the person is often ___ to communicate a need': after 'is' and before 'to + verb', we need a verb ending in -ing.
The idea is that the unusual behaviour is the person's effort to tell us something.
'trying to communicate' gives that meaning.
The answer is 'trying'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (52) with a suitable word.

explanation: The sentence has two halves: 'dementia affects the brain' and 'they may find it difficult to express themselves'.
The first half is the reason for the second. A connector of reason that can start a sentence is needed: As, Because or Since.
Remember the capital letter at the start of the sentence.
The answer is 'As'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (53) with a suitable word.

explanation: Read the sentences before it: a person with dementia who behaves in an unusual way is often 'trying to communicate a need or feeling'.
So behaviour is being used to say what words cannot. The sentence explains why: it is difficult for them to express themselves with words alone.
'only with words' gives this meaning. An adverb that says how well they express themselves, such as 'clearly', also makes good sense here.
The key's answer is 'only'.

review.note: The key gives 'only' (the same word as blank 48). The solved answer was 'clearly'. Both make sense: 'only/solely with words' (words alone are not enough) or 'clearly/properly/well with words'. The key's word is the model answer and the others are accepted; a school marker may be stricter.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (54) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'even though they have ___ eaten': the blank sits between 'have' and the past participle 'eaten'.
'even though' shows a contrast: they ask for food again when the meal is over. The adverb that shows something is done before now is 'already'.
The answer is 'already'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (55) with a suitable word.

explanation: After 'cannot' we need a base verb, and after the blank is 'having their meal'.
Why would someone ask for food straight after eating? Because the memory of the meal is gone. Paragraph 1 says dementia causes problems with memory.
'recall' and 'remember' both mean to bring a memory back, and both can be followed by a verb ending in -ing.
The answer is 'recall' (or 'remember').

questions.stem: Fill in blank (56) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'some may stay ___ at night and feel sleepy during the day': the second half is the result of the first.
People feel sleepy in the day when they have not slept at night. 'stay awake' means not to sleep.
'stay up' means the same.
The answer is 'awake'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (57) with a suitable word.

explanation: The sentence before says a person with dementia 'may use the **wrong** word'.
So what they are trying to find is the opposite: the right words.
'to find the right words' is a common phrase. 'correct' means the same.
The answer is 'right'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (58) with a suitable word.

explanation: This is a fixed phrase: to **pay attention to** something means to notice it and think about it carefully.
'paying ___ to the person's emotions': the verb 'pay' and the preposition 'to' on either side of the blank are the clues.
The answer is 'attention'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (59) with a suitable word.

explanation: The blank comes before the noun 'concerns', so it needs a possessive word. Whose concerns? Those of people with dementia.
The rest of the sentence uses 'they' and 'their' for them: 'how **they** feel' and '**their** unmet needs'.
Keep the pronoun the same throughout.
The answer is 'their'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (60) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'offer reassurance when ___.' The sentence ends at the blank, so this is a short form of 'when it is ___'.
Caregivers cannot reassure someone every second; they do it at the moments the person is upset or confused, that is, when it is needed.
'when needed' and 'when necessary' are common short forms.
The answer is 'needed'.

questions.stem:
Jade admired her grandfather as he was wise.
____________________ because of ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: Jade admired her grandfather because of his wisdom.

explanation: 'because of' must be followed by a noun or noun phrase, not a clause. 'because of he was wise' is wrong.
Change the adjective 'wise' to its noun, 'wisdom'.
Change the subject 'he' to the possessive 'his' to show whose wisdom it was: 'his wisdom'.
Keep the first part as it is. Answer: Jade admired her grandfather because of his wisdom.

review.keyAnswer: Jill admired her grandfather because of his wisdom.
review.solvedAnswer: Jade admired her grandfather because of his wisdom.
review.note: The key writes 'Jill' for the name; the question says 'Jade'. This is a slip in the key (Jill is the name in Q64). The answer is otherwise the same.

questions.stem:
Both the bicycle shops in the park are closed today.
Neither of ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: Neither of the bicycle shops in the park is open today.

explanation: 'Neither of' is negative: it means 'not one and not the other'. To keep the meaning, the rest of the sentence must change to its opposite: 'closed' becomes 'open'. ('Neither ... is closed' would mean both are open.)
After 'Neither of' use 'the' + plural noun: 'Neither of the bicycle shops'.
Agreement rule: 'Neither of ...' takes a singular verb in formal writing, so 'are' becomes 'is'.
Answer: Neither of the bicycle shops in the park is open today.

review.keyAnswer: Neither of the bicycle shops in the park is open today.
review.solvedAnswer: Neither of the bicycle shops in the park is open today.

questions.stem:
The electrician fixed the lights. They now work perfectly.
____________________ as a result of ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: The lights work perfectly now as a result of the electrician fixing them.
accept: The lights now work perfectly as a result of the electrician fixing them.
The lights work perfectly now as a result of the electrician's fixing them.
The lights now work perfectly as a result of the electrician's fixing them.
The lights now work perfectly as a result of the electrician having fixed them.
The lights work perfectly now as a result of the electrician having fixed them.

explanation: 'as a result of' is followed by the **cause**, so the result comes first: the lights work perfectly (result) as a result of the fixing (cause).
Replace 'They' with 'The lights', because the lights have not been mentioned yet in the new sentence.
'as a result of' ends in a preposition, so it must be followed by a noun or a verb ending in -ing, not a clause. 'as a result of the electrician fixed them' is wrong; change 'fixed' to 'fixing'.
Use 'them' to avoid repeating 'the lights'. Answer: The lights work perfectly now as a result of the electrician fixing them.

review.keyAnswer: The lights work perfectly now as a result of the electrician fixing them.
review.solvedAnswer: The lights work perfectly now as a result of the electrician fixing them.

questions.stem:
"Did you remember to return the library book?" Jill asked Jack.
Jill asked Jack if ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: Jill asked Jack if he had remembered to return the library book.

explanation: This is direct speech changed to reported speech. A reported yes/no question uses 'if', statement word order (subject before verb), no 'did', and a full stop instead of a question mark.
Tense moves one step back: simple past 'Did you remember' becomes past perfect 'had remembered'.
Pronouns change to fit the people: 'you' is Jack, so 'he'.
'to return the library book' stays the same. Answer: Jill asked Jack if he had remembered to return the library book.

review.keyAnswer: Jill asked Jack if he had remembered to return the library book.
review.solvedAnswer: Jill asked Jack if he had remembered to return the library book.

questions.stem:
My aunt was upset about the rude staff. She complained to the manager.
____________________ and made ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: My aunt was upset about the rude staff and made a complaint to the manager.

explanation: The given words 'and made' need an object: you 'make' a thing. So the verb 'complained' must become its noun, 'complaint'.
'complaint' is a singular countable noun, so it needs an article: 'made **a** complaint'.
Both actions have the same subject, 'My aunt', so 'She' is dropped after 'and'.
Watch the spelling: complain (verb), complain**t** (noun). Answer: My aunt was upset about the rude staff and made a complaint to the manager.

review.keyAnswer: My aunt was upset about the rude staff and made a complaint to the manager.
review.solvedAnswer: My aunt was upset about the rude staff and made a complaint to the manager.

questions.stem: Based on paragraph 1, why did Darto cause trouble and chase chickens?

answer.value: He was bored because life in the quiet village moved too slowly for him and his imagination.

explanation: Find the sentence about Darto in paragraph 1: 'Life moved slowly in their quiet village—far too slowly for Darto, whose imagination could power a small city.'
A boy with a huge imagination in a place where nothing happens gets bored, so he made his own excitement by causing trouble and chasing chickens.
The marker looks for the cause: life in the village was too slow or quiet for Darto (he was bored). Do not just repeat that he liked chasing chickens.

review.keyAnswer: He was bored because life in the quiet village moved too slowly for his imagination.
review.solvedAnswer: Life in the quiet village moved too slowly for him, so he was bored. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: What were two things that Darto did to make sure he was not seen by Uncle Banu?

answer.value: He crept quietly into Uncle Banu's yard, and he made his move only when he saw the lights in the house go out.

explanation: Look at paragraph 4, where Darto goes to Uncle Banu's yard at night.
First thing: he 'crept quietly into Uncle Banu's yard'. To creep is to move slowly and silently so as not to be noticed.
Second thing: after the lights came on he 'kept an eye on the house and made his move only when he saw the lights go out'. He waited until Uncle Banu was no longer up and about.
One mark for each action. 'Darto froze' on its own is weaker, because freezing was a reaction of fright; the waiting for the lights to go out is the action that kept him from being seen.

review.keyAnswer: He crept quietly into the yard and moved only after the house lights had gone out.
review.solvedAnswer: He crept quietly into the yard; he waited and moved only when the lights went out. Agrees with key.

questions.stem:
Based on the information from lines 11-12 (paragraph 4, from "He kept an eye" to "as harmless as possible"), complete the following table.
(For each action, write its purpose.)

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Action: hands stretched out towards it
Purpose:
explanation: The sentence is 'Darto walked slowly towards Putih, his hands stretched out towards it, trying to appear as harmless as possible.'
Why would he reach out with his hands? His whole plan was to catch the chicken ('Catching Putih will be easy!'), and hands are what you grab with.
The purpose is to catch Putih.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt:
Action: trying to appear as harmless as possible
Purpose:

answer.value: So that he would not frighten Putih away.

explanation: 'harmless' means not likely to hurt anyone. Darto wanted to look as if he meant no harm.
If Putih sensed danger it would run off before he got close. The next paragraph shows exactly that: 'as though realising his true intentions, Putih bolted'.
The purpose is to stop Putih from being frightened and running away (so that he could get close enough).

review.keyAnswer: (a) To catch Putih. (b) So that he would not frighten Putih away.
review.solvedAnswer: a) to grab/catch Putih; b) so that Putih would not be scared off. Agrees with key.

questions.stem:
Fill in the table below with how Darto felt and explain why he felt that way. The first row has been filled in for you.

When Darto first learnt about Putin — How Darto felt: **Excited**. Why he felt that way: **If he caught Putin, everyone would admit he was the best chicken chaser in the village.**
(The table on the paper prints "Putin"; it means Putih, the chicken.)

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
When the lights in Uncle Banu's house turned on
(Write how Darto felt, then why he felt that way.)

answer.value: Frightened. He feared that Uncle Banu would spot (catch) him in the yard.

explanation: Find the moment in paragraph 4: 'Just then, the lights in Uncle Banu's house turned on. Darto froze, his heart beating so fast he thought it might burst.'
Freezing and a pounding heart are signs of fear. Words such as frightened, afraid, scared or terrified fit.
Why? The lights meant Uncle Banu might be awake and might see him sneaking in the yard at night.
One mark for the feeling and one for the reason.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt:
After he failed to catch Putin the first time
(Write how Darto felt, then why he felt that way.)

answer.value: Embarrassed. He had boasted that catching Putih would be easy, but he failed and his friends laughed at him.

explanation: Find the moment in paragraph 6, just after the failed chase: Arif and Siti 'were laughing so hard they could barely breathe. Cheeks burning, Darto glared at his friends'.
'Cheeks burning' shows a red face, a sign of embarrassment (humiliated or ashamed also fit).
Why? In paragraph 3 he had boasted, 'Catching Putih will be easy!' Now he had failed in front of his friends, and Siti shouted, 'I told you he couldn't do it!'
One mark for the feeling and one for the reason (he had boasted but failed, and his friends laughed at him).

review.keyAnswer: (a) Frightened – he feared Uncle Banu would spot him in the yard. (b) Embarrassed – he had boasted that catching Putih would be easy, but failed and his friends laughed at him.
review.solvedAnswer: a) frightened of being caught by Uncle Banu; b) embarrassed because his friends laughed at his failure. Agrees with key.
review.note: The table on the paper misprints the chicken's name as 'Putin' three times (the passage says 'Putih'). It is transcribed as printed, with a bracketed line telling the child it means Putih. The 4 marks are split 2 per row (1 for the feeling, 1 for the reason).

questions.stem: In what way was Putih cleverer than Darto? Find evidence from lines 13-18 (paragraph 5) to support your answer.

answer.value: Putih outsmarted Darto by deliberately leading him into a muddy ditch and then through a thorny bush, which left him exhausted, bleeding and coated in mud (while Putih got away).

explanation: Find 'cleverer' in paragraph 5: 'the chicken was faster—and far cleverer. It **led him** into a muddy ditch, then through a thorny bush that left his arms covered in scratches.'
'led him' shows Putih chose where to run. It picked places that were easy for a small bird but hard and painful for a boy.
The result proves it worked: 'By the time he emerged, he was exhausted, bleeding and coated in mud', and Putih had not been caught.

The marker looks for: (1) the way it was cleverer: it tricked or outsmarted Darto by leading him through difficult places; (2) the evidence: the muddy ditch and the thorny bush, and the state Darto ended up in.

review.keyAnswer: Putih outsmarted Darto by deliberately leading him into a muddy ditch and through a thorny bush, leaving him exhausted, bleeding and covered in mud.
review.solvedAnswer: It led him into a muddy ditch and through a thorny bush so that he ended up exhausted, bleeding and muddy while it escaped. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: Which 2-word phrase from lines 19-23 (paragraph 6) shows that Putih knew it had beaten Darto?

explanation: In paragraph 6, find where Putih is described: 'then at the Putih, who was **perched smugly** on the roof of Uncle Banu's goat shed'.
'smugly' means in a way that shows you are very pleased with yourself, usually because you have won or done better than someone else.
A chicken sitting calmly up on a roof, looking pleased with itself, shows it knew it had won.
Copy exactly two words: perched (1) smugly (2).

questions.stem: Based on the lines 24-44 (paragraphs 7 to 13), state whether each statement in the table below is true or false, then give one reason why you think so.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Putih attacked and hurt Darto.
(Type True or False, then give one reason from the passage.)

answer.value: False. Putih launched itself at Darto with its claws outstretched, but Darto dodged and ran, so he was not hurt.

explanation: Paragraph 8: 'with a loud squawk, it launched itself at Darto, claws outstretched. Darto **dodged** and ran for his life.'
The statement has two halves. 'attacked' is right, but 'hurt' is not: to dodge is to move quickly out of the way, so the claws never touched him. After that the chicken only 'chased him'.
When one half of a statement is wrong, the whole statement is False.
Reason: Darto dodged Putih's attack (and ran away), so he was not hurt.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt:
Darto did not expect the crowd to be there.
(Type True or False, then give one reason from the passage.)

answer.value: True. Word of his mission had spread through the village without Darto knowing ("Unknown to Darto"), and a crowd had gathered.

explanation: Paragraph 7: 'he saw a crowd of children. **Unknown to Darto**, word of his mission had spread through the village thanks to Arif and Siti.'
'Unknown to Darto' means he had no idea that people had been told, so he could not have expected a crowd.
The statement is True. Reason: he did not know that word of his mission had spread through the village.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt:
Darto gave up on catching Putih completely.
(Type True or False, then give one reason from the passage.)

answer.value: False. Darto made several more attempts to catch Putih.

explanation: Paragraph 13: 'Trying to catch Putih became something of a tradition among the children after that. Even Darto made **several more attempts**.'
The trap is paragraph 9, where Darto 'was finally ready to admit defeat'. That was only for that day. The word 'completely' in the statement makes it false, because he tried again later.
The statement is False. Reason: Darto made several more attempts to catch Putih.

review.keyAnswer: (a) False - Putih launched itself at Darto, but Darto dodged it, so he was not hurt. (b) True – word had spread through the village without Darto knowing, and a crowd gathered. (c) False – Darto made several more attempts to catch Putih.
review.solvedAnswer: a) False (he dodged); b) True ('Unknown to Darto'); c) False (several more attempts). Agrees with key.

questions.stem:
Write 1, 2 and 3 in the blanks below to indicate the order in which the events occurred in the story.

____ Putih chased Darto.
____ Darto felt nervous.
____ Arif and Siti told everyone about Darto's mission.

(Type the three numbers in the order of the statements above, from top to bottom, for example 1, 2, 3.)

explanation: Find each event in the passage, then put them in time order. Be careful: the order in which the passage mentions things is not always the order in which they happened.

Arif and Siti told everyone: paragraph 7 says 'word of his mission **had spread** through the village thanks to Arif and Siti'. 'had spread' shows this happened before Darto reached the yard and saw the crowd. This is event 1.
Darto felt nervous: also paragraph 7, 'Darto's stomach fluttered at the sight of so many eyes on him.' He felt this when he saw the crowd. This is event 2.
Putih chased Darto: paragraphs 8 and 9, after he threw the net and missed. This is event 3.
Reading the statements from top to bottom, the numbers are 3, 2, 1.

questions.stem: Look at the table below. What do the words in the left column refer to in the passage? Write your answers in the column on the right.

parts.label: a
explanation: Line 19 is Siti's shout: 'I told you he couldn't do **it**!'
'it' points back to the thing Darto had set out to do. In paragraph 3 he boasted, 'Catching Putih will be easy!', and paragraph 5 describes how he failed.
Test by replacing the word: 'I told you he couldn't catch Putih!' It makes sense.
The answer is catching Putih. Here 'it' is an action, not the chicken itself.

parts.label: b

answer.value: The crowd of children (and Uncle Banu) who had come to the chicken yard to watch him.
accept: the crowd of children and uncle banu

explanation: Line 28: 'However, Darto waved to **his audience**'. An audience is a group of people watching something.
Look back in the same paragraph for who was watching: 'he saw a crowd of children', 'They cheered him on', 'Even Uncle Banu was there', 'so many eyes on him'.
The answer is the crowd of children, and Uncle Banu, who had gathered at the chicken yard to watch Darto. Writing only 'Arif and Siti' is not enough.

review.keyAnswer: (a) catching Putih (b) the crowd of children and Uncle Banu
review.solvedAnswer: a) catching Putih; b) the crowd of children (and Uncle Banu) at the chicken yard. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: Explain clearly why Putih was considered a legend in the village.

answer.value: No one in the village could catch Putih, not even Darto after several attempts, and trying to catch it became a tradition among the village children.

explanation: A legend is someone or something famous for being extraordinary, that people keep talking about. Look for what made Putih extraordinary and what shows it became famous.

Extraordinary: nobody could catch it. Arif calls it 'a chicken that cannot be caught', it was 'no ordinary chicken', and Darto 'never did catch Putih'. It was also very old: Uncle Banu's grandfather 'raised it from an egg'.
Famous: 'Trying to catch Putih became something of a tradition among the children after that.'
The marker looks for two points: (1) no one could catch Putih; (2) trying to catch it became a tradition among the children of the village.

review.keyAnswer: No one in the village could catch Putih, and trying to catch it became a tradition among the village children.
review.solvedAnswer: Nobody could ever catch Putih (and it was unusually old), and trying to catch it became a tradition among the children. Agrees with key.

questions.stem:
The pictures below show Tom, Siti and Devi having a conversation. Study the pictures carefully.
[[img1]]
++Your Task++
Imagine you are Tom.
**Write an email to your teacher, Miss Hanisah, to share about the class community service project you and your classmates have discussed.**
You are to refer to the pictures and information above for your email. The bullet point underlined below requires you to come up with your own information.

In your email, include the following key information:
• the name of the community service project
• what your class will make and its purpose
• the art materials required
• the date by which you hope to get the materials
• ++one value your class can learn from this project++

You may reorder the points. Remember to write in complete sentences.

images.alt: Two rows of pictures showing Tom, Siti and Devi talking in a library. Top row. Tom: After our examinations, we should organise a class community service project. Let's fold 1,000 paper cranes to cheer up the patients at Rainbow Hospital! Siti: Great idea, Tom! We can call it 'Project Paper Crane' or 'Fold a Crane, Bring a Smile'! Devi: Let's use Siti's second suggestion. We'll need coloured paper. We won't need glue, but we will need some nylon string to hang the paper cranes. Bottom row. Tom: I'll email Miss Hanisah to tell her about our class community service project and ask her to help us get the art materials by 15 September. Siti: No. We must get the materials by 10 September so that we will have enough time to fold the cranes. Devi: You should explain why our class is doing this as our community service project and the values we can learn from this project.

answer.value: There is no single model answer. Check your writing against the points below.

explanation: Purpose: to tell Miss Hanisah about the class community service project and to ask for her help in getting the art materials. Say this clearly near the start of the email.
Audience and tone: Miss Hanisah is your teacher, so the email is formal and polite. Begin 'Dear Miss Hanisah', use full sentences, and avoid short forms and slang.
Context: you are Tom, writing for your class after discussing the project with Siti and Devi. Write as 'I' and 'we'.
Point 1, name of the project: 'Fold a Crane, Bring a Smile'. Devi chose Siti's **second** suggestion, so 'Project Paper Crane' is wrong.
Point 2, what the class will make and its purpose: 1,000 paper cranes, to cheer up the patients at Rainbow Hospital. Give both the item and the purpose.
Point 3, art materials required: coloured paper and nylon string (to hang the paper cranes). Do not ask for glue; Devi said it is not needed.
Point 4, date: by 10 September, so that there is enough time to fold the cranes. Tom's '15 September' was corrected by Siti.

Point 5, your own information: one value the class can learn, with a short reason, for example compassion (caring for people who are ill), teamwork (working together to fold 1,000 cranes) or perseverance.

Format: a greeting, a short opening that states the purpose, the points in a sensible order, a polite closing line such as thanking her for her help, then 'Yours sincerely' or 'Regards' and the name Tom.
Marks: 14 in all, for task fulfilment (all five points, correct details, purpose, audience and context) and for language (grammar, spelling, punctuation and organisation).

questions.stem:
Write a composition of ++at least 150 words++ about **making the best of a situation**.

The pictures are provided to help you think about this topic.
Your composition should be based on one or more of these pictures.
[[img1]]
Consider the following points when you plan your composition:
• What was the situation?
• How did you make the best of the situation?

You may use the points in any order and include other relevant points as well.

images.alt: Three pictures, one above the other. Picture 1: a boy with a sad face leaning on a window sill, looking out at heavy rain. Picture 2: a sign hanging from a hook that says 'SORRY, THIS EVENT IS CANCELLED'. Picture 3: a hand holding a mobile phone whose screen shows a crossed-out Wi-Fi symbol and the words 'NO INTERNET CONNECTION'.

answer.value: There is no single model answer. Check your writing against the points below.

explanation: Understand the topic: 'making the best of a situation' means something disappointing or difficult happened that you could not change, and you chose to do something good with it instead of sulking. The story needs both halves: the bad situation and the positive response.
Picture 1 (boy at a rainy window): rain spoils an outing, a match or a picnic. Making the best of it could be an indoor picnic, board games with a grandparent, or baking together.

Picture 2 (event cancelled sign): a concert, camp, party or competition is called off. Making the best of it could be holding your own small version, using the time to help someone, or finding something new to enjoy.

Picture 3 (no internet connection): the Wi-Fi goes down during the holidays or before an online activity. Making the best of it could be rediscovering books, playing outside with neighbours, or really talking to your family.
Use one or more pictures. One picture developed well is better than three squeezed in.

Story arc: an opening that shows what you were looking forward to; the problem (the let-down and how you felt); a turning point where you, or someone who inspired you, decided to make the best of it; what you did; the result.
Show the change in feelings: disappointment or frustration at first, then determination, then surprise at how well things turned out. Use actions, speech and thoughts to show them.
Ending: return to the topic. Reflect on what you learnt, for example that you cannot control what happens but you can control how you respond.
Check: at least 150 words, paragraphs, a consistent past tense, varied sentence openings and precise vocabulary. Marks: 36 in all, for content and for language and organisation.

review.keyAnswer: No key is given for Paper 1.
review.solvedAnswer: Planning checklist written from the topic and the three pictures.
